evaluation_locator: Appendix A.1 pp.16-17; C.1-C.2 pp.20-21; Section 4.1 p.6.
resource_reporting: Training/inference hardware and retrieval/beam budgets: four 80GB A100 GPUs for training; one or two 24GB Quadro RTX6000 GPUs for inference; beam 2 and retrieval thresholds. Retrieval-frequency sweep is reported; measured wall-clock latency not located in inspected sections.

caveat: S&P denominator is conditional on the model support/relevance decisions. Reflection agreement with GPT-4 is not independent truth adjudication. Citation recall concerns generated claims, not all information a user requires.

role: Mitigation: prompted verification and response revision
inspected_sections: Sections 3-4 and Limitations (PDF pp.3-9); Appendix Sections 6-8/Tables 4-6 (pp.12-13). Formal Findings ACL 2024 proceedings version.
reference_frame: world-factuality operationalized via entity/QA labels and retrieval-based biography FActScore (Section 4.1 p.5)
scoring_unit: mixed: verification questions/atomic facts or entities, final response factual precision/count and span F1/recall (Sections 3-4 pp.3-8)
evidence_and_access: Black-box language generation: draft, plan verification questions, answer them, revise. Main procedure reuses LLaMA-65B across stages; factored verification hides the draft and answers questions separately, without external retrieval in the correction steps (Sections 3.1-3.4 pp.3-4; 4.2 p.5).
information_control: Correct/incorrect entity counts, multi-span precision/recall/F1, biography fact count with FActScore. Same-generator biography result 55.9 to 71.4 FActScore accompanies 16.6 to 12.3 facts. A separate Llama-2-chat clipping control is not a matched-length CoVe control.
evaluation_separation: Same generator performs draft, verification and revision; prompt isolation reduces direct draft conditioning but proves no error independence. Gold entity/QA labels and retrieval-based FActScore score final answers; these are not the same procedure as CoVe verification.
resource_reporting: Worst-case LLM-call formula for factor+revise is 1+s+2f, with s response sentences and f verification questions; verification can be parallelized. Measured deployment latency or equal-token-budget comparison not located in inspected sections.
joint_validation: related component analysis: verification-question accuracy/formats, final generation metrics and SelfCheckGPT filtering comparison. Fixed-detector calibration on pre/post revision output under matched information not located in inspected sections.
joint_locator: Section 4.3 p.8; Appendix Sections 6 and 8/Tables 4 and 6 pp.12-13.
caveat: Precision gain does not establish preservation of all correct or required facts. Closed-book checks remain bounded by model knowledge; shorter output is a measured trade-off, not proof of the entire gain being due to deletion.

role: Mitigation: tool-assisted critique and iterative correction
inspected_sections: Sections 3-4 (PDF pp.3-9); Appendix A (p.21), C.3 (p.23), D.1-D.5 (pp.24-27). Formal ICLR 2024 proceedings version.
reference_frame: mixed: free-form QA correctness as world-factuality proxy, mathematical answer correctness, and a separate toxicity task (Sections 4.1-4.3 pp.5-9)
scoring_unit: mixed: response/answer EM and F1; response confidence; program correctness; output toxicity (Section 4 pp.5-9; Appendix D.1 p.24)
evidence_and_access: Black-box generator with Google/web feedback for QA, Python execution for math, Perspective API for toxicity; iterative critique/correction uses the generator itself (Section 3 pp.3-5). QA uses up to 7 tool interactions and 3 correction iterations (Section 4.1 pp.5-6).
information_control: QA EM/F1 and qualitative/manual refusal and incorrect-correction categories; math answer correctness; toxicity task reports fluency/diversity proxies. No matched answered-question coverage or required-aspect preservation located. Non-oracle CRITIC and oracle CRITIC* must be kept separate.
evaluation_separation: QA correction consults web evidence, but final evaluation uses dataset answers; manual 100-case HotpotQA analysis identifies matching/label errors. Detection labels use answer F1>0.6. In the separate toxicity task, Perspective API is reused as feedback and final evaluator.
evaluation_locator: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 pp.5-9; Appendix D.1-D.2 pp.24-26.
resource_reporting: Interaction/iteration budgets and qualitative latency growth are stated; Appendix D.3 reports approximately 9GB cached Jan-Apr 2023 web results and no tool subscription charges. This does not mean LLM inference/API calls are free or measured equal-cost latency.
resource_locator: Section 4.1 pp.5-6; Appendix A p.21; Appendix D.3 p.26.
joint_validation: related component analysis: explicit self-verification ACC/AUROC on initial CoT answers, correction results on the same QA splits, and manual correction-error analysis. This is not a fixed-detector before/after correction robustness matrix.
joint_locator: Appendix D.1/Table 5 pp.24-25; D.2/Tables 6-7 pp.25-26; Section 4.1/Table 1 pp.5-6.
caveat: Table 6 error-type percentages have a less explicit denominator than a full transition matrix; do not treat 10% incorrect correction as the population rate. Oracle CRITIC* is not deployable verification; math/toxicity results do not directly measure factual hallucination.
